\caption{Ruleset-size scalability (input fixed), per folding step, on \textsc{ClamAV} (left) and \textsc{MS-DLP} (right). \emph{Top:} absolute circuit size with the single-rule framework floor (dotted; $10.69$\,M R1CS for \textsc{ClamAV}, $0.13$\,M for \textsc{MS-DLP}); growing the ruleset to the full $38{,}875$ (\textsc{ClamAV}) / $987$ (\textsc{MS-DLP}) rules grows the circuit far slower than the rule count. \emph{Bottom:} net circuit cost \emph{per rule per input byte}---cumulative R1CS above the floor divided by cumulative rule count times per-step input length---falling from $1.36\times10^{-3}$ to $0.78\times10^{-3}$ (\ttt{gdb}) and $0.79\times10^{-3}$ to $0.42\times10^{-3}$ (\ttt{readelf}) R1CS per rule-byte (\textsc{ClamAV}) and $1334.28\times10^{-3}$ to $1334.28\times10^{-3}$ (\ttt{email1}) and $323.59\times10^{-3}$ to $16.03\times10^{-3}$ (\ttt{email2}) R1CS per rule-byte (\textsc{MS-DLP}) at the full set.
